text:
sara: Proposal: add a 'bindings' field to service-account tokens so we can attach route-level routing/quotas and more precise telemetry. Think: token metadata -> { org, project, sa, bindings: [{route:"/v1/generate", quota_group:"chat-small"}, ...] }

kyle: curious — does this mean tokens carry policy decisions? can we still do runtime routing without exploding token churn?

sara: good q. plan is tokens are lightweight references to policies stored in auth DB. bindings can be either embedded (for short-lived tokens) or reference ids. runtime routing reads policy id. fallback to existing routing if policy missing.

matt: from infra POV need to know cache invalidation for policy changes. if we add policy refs we need TTLs and a push invalidation channel to runtimes. otherwise stale routing/quotas.

jamie: security catch: if tokens can embed route bindings we need strict signing + aud claims. We should avoid embedding arbitrary quotas in tokens unless they are short-lived. Also audit trail must show which policy was evaluated at request time.

olivia-bot: deploy-bot: new auth-config PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/auth/pulls/402

kyle: also want to map this to console UX. Product asked for "per-route quota visibility" in the console. We need unique stable ids for bindings so console dashboards can drill into usage.

sara: agreed. proposal: policy object has id, name, description, route_matchers, quota_key. console will display quota_key and associated per-token usage.

matt: telemetry question: do we tag each request with policy_id and token_owner (org/project/sa) or do we correlate by token hash? tagging policy_id is simplest, but leaking policy_id may be sensitive?

jamie: policy_id is fine as long as it's an internal opaque id. For logs we should never include full token. Store token hash in audit logs for correlation.

kyle: rollout strategy? can't change tokens for everyone overnight. need backward-compatible proposal: if token has bindings -> honor; if token references policy id -> lookup; else -> legacy mapping.

sara: yep. migration plan: 1) support policy refs + binding embed for short lived tokens; 2) opt-in console UI to create policy refs; 3) ramp usage and then start migrating long-lived tokens with grace period.

matt: will need metrics to track how many requests hit legacy path vs new policy path. add a simple counter: auth.policy.eval.path = {legacy|embedded|ref}.

jamie: also add regression monitors: e.g., quota enforcement delta per org during rollout. If enforcement mismatch > threshold, auto rollback.

olivia-bot: incident-bot: created ticket AUTH-211: monitor-policy-rollout (owner: matt)

kyle: dev-ops detail: routing should still support runtime fallback to model variant when quota denies. example: route-policy -> allow but quota exhausted -> fallback to smaller model. Want to ensure policy evaluation returns structured decisions: {allow: true, quota_status: "ok"|"exhausted", fallback: "model-small"} so runtime can act.

sara: nice. ensure decision object is compact to keep latency low. we should bench policy lookup + decision cost (p50 target < 2ms).

matt: I'll prototype a local LRU plus push invalidation + streaming updates. if policy refs are common we can cache heavily.

jamie: DB schema: policy table with id (uuid), org_id, project_id, matcher json (text), quota_key, created_by, version. Need version increments for safe rollback.

kyle: console UX: small flow — create policy -> attach to SA token (or generate new token bound to policy) -> view per-policy telemetry. Add warning when attaching to long-lived tokens.

sara: outstanding items: 1) spec for token metadata (embed vs ref) 2) policy evaluation API (sync low-latency and async audit logs) 3) cache/invalidation design 4) console changes + migration plan 5) metrics/alerts.

matt: I'll add a draft cache/invalidation doc in the PR.

jamie: security will review token spec and audit requirements. prefer short-lived tokens for embedded bindings by default.

kyle: can someone sketch the token metadata example?

sara: sure — example:```json
{
  "iss":"redwood",
  "sub":"sa:1234",
  "org":"org_9a1",
  "project":"proj_7b2",
  "exp":1680000000,
  "bindings_ref":"policy:9f8a7b6c",
  "hash":"sha256:..."
}
```

matt: for embedded example:```json
{
  "sub":"sa:1234",
  "bindings":[{"route":"/v1/embeddings","quota_group":"embed-small"}],
  "exp":1680000100
}
```

jamie: quick checklist from sec: token signing alg, minimum TTL for embedded bindings, audit consistency, admin revoke path.

sara: thanks. next: I'll draft the high-level design doc and post in #eng-platform for review tomorrow. @kyle @matt @jamie please comment on AUTH-211 and the PR. :thumbsup:
